# Obsidian Notes for DeepSeek Harness
**A local Obsidian-style notes pane for the DeepSeek Harness web UI.** Point it at a folder of Markd
own files, then read, edit, search and cite them next to the conversation — without opening Obsidian
, without importing anything, and without your notes leaving the machine.
English | 中文
## What it does

A local-first Markdown notes panel that sits in the DSH sidebar and hands notes
to the chat without

st Markdown notes panel that sits in the DSH sidebar and hands notes
to the chat without copy-paste:

1. **Your notes stay beside the conversation.** Point it at a folder of Markdown
files and you get t

he vault tree, a line-numbered Obsidian-flavoured preview,
edit/save, and search across titles and b

odies — no import, no sync, no cloud.
2. **The handoff is the feature.** Cite a whole note as an `@p

ath` mention, or
select a passage and press **Ask** — the prompt in the composer carries the
absolut

e path, the line range and the quoted text, so the model can refer to
exactly what you read.
3. **Sc

reenshots become part of the vault.** Paste an image while editing and it
is saved into the attachme

nt folder as an Obsidian-native
`![[Pasted image …]]` embed; moving that folder later rewrites the e

mbeds.
4. **Two ways to see the shape of a vault.** Turn a note into a **mind map**
built from its h

eadings and list items, or open the **relation graph**
computed from `[[links]]` and `#tags` — vault

-wide, or locally around the open
note with 1–5 hops.

Everything runs on your machine: the plugin reads and writes only the folder you
choose, and the cli
ent talks to the host over its own loopback routes.
## Features

- **Vault sidebar** — lazy directory tree; open a note with one click, create,
rename or delete note

s and folders, and search titles **and** file contents.
Shows a live note count.
- **Line-numbered O

bsidian preview** — every source line keeps its line number.
Real tables with alignment, fenced code

with language labels, nested lists and
task lists, all heading levels, setext headings, horizontal

rules, and
clickable `[[wikilinks]]` (aliases and `#sections` included). Inline Obsidian
styles rend

er too: `==highlight==`, `~~strikethrough~~`, backslash escapes,
hidden `%%comments%%`, and `<https:

//…>` / bare URLs as links.
- **Graph view** — a vault-wide relation graph built from every note's `

[[links]]`
and `#tags` (no graph file, no export step: it is computed from your Markdown on
the fly,

like Obsidian's own graph). A vault-level entry above the note tree
opens it as its own view; scrol

l to zoom, drag to pan, hover to highlight
neighbours, click a note to open it in the dock. **Local*

* shows the
neighbourhood of the note that is currently open; the depth is adjustable
from 1 to 5 ho

ps (same range as Obsidian's local graph depth slider, default
1), and **Focus current note** jumps

from the vault view straight to it.
- **Mind map view** — toggle the preview into a horizontal mind

map built from the
note's headings and list items. Scroll to zoom, drag to pan; select a node to
jum

p to its source line, or insert that whole branch (node + descendants) into
the chat as context. Ren

dering only — the Markdown file is untouched.
- **Callouts** — `> [!type] title` blocks render with

type colours, icons and
badges. 13 canonical types (`note`, `abstract`, `info`, `todo`, `tip`,
`succ

ess`, `question`, `warning`, `failure`, `danger`, `bug`, `example`,
`quote`) plus 15 Obsidian aliase

s (`summary`, `tldr`, `hint`, `important`,
`check`, `done`, `help`, `faq`, `caution`, `attention`, `

fail`, `missing`,
`error`, `cite`, `none`).
- **Edit and save** — line-numbered source editor, save

with the button or

## Security and privacy

- **Local only, no telemetry.** The plugin serves everything from the DSH host's
own `/obsidian/*` r

outes. It makes no outbound network requests and contains
no analytics. (Links you click in a note a

re ordinary links; the plugin does
not fetch them.)
- **Behind the DSH auth fence.** The routes are

mounted on the DSH web server, so
they require the same authenticated session/token as the app. On t
ts are exempt only because `` tags cannot set headers (they are still behind the app's auth). -

**Vault containment.** Every path that crosses the route boundary is
normalized first (absolute pat

hs, `..`, backslashes and drive letters are
rejected) and then re-checked with `realpath` against th

e resolved vault root,
so symlinks cannot escape either. Setting the attachment folder outside the
v

ault is rejected with `403`.
- **Explicit limits.** A single note is capped at 1 MB, a pasted image

at
20 MB, and a search at 4000 scanned files / 100 results.
- **Destructive actions are scoped.**
-

Deleting a note or folder requires confirmation and deletes only the vault
entry (folders recursivel

y).
- Deleting sessions removes only that session's log directory under
`$DSH_HOME/sessions` and its

projection cache under `$DSH_HOME/storages`;
running sessions (including running subagents) are ref

used, and symlinked
directories are skipped. Archiving is one-way: the log stays on disk.
- Deleting

a workspace removes its registration and its session logs — the
directory and files are kept.
- **N

o hidden writes.** The only write paths are: a note save, the attachment
upload, attachment folder m

igration, orphan cleanup (opt-in), and session-log
deletion you initiated.
## Compatibility

- **DSH:** verified against **0.2.1-rc.5** (web UI, desktop app shell). The
composer integration tar

gets DSH 0.2's Lexical input and falls back to the
0.1.x textarea path where possible.
- **Node.js:*

* `^22.19 || >=24` (needed only when running the host from source).
- **OS:** paths are handled with

the platform separator; session paths use
`$DSH_HOME`. The screenshots above were captured on macOS

.
- **Not rendered** (kept as source text): math, mermaid, footnotes, tags, raw
HTML, note transclus

ion, audio/PDF embeds, block refs (`^id`), callout
folding/unknown types/nested callouts, and some i

nline emphasis edge cases
(`***bold italic***`, nested emphasis, `_` next to text).
